summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted after experiencing sudden generalized weakness, confusion, and slurred speech during a car ride, which resolved by the time he reached the emergency department. Given his history of mechanical aortic valve and prior strokes, concern was high for a transient ischemic attack (TIA). His INR was subtherapeutic at 1.8, increasing stroke risk. A head CT showed no acute infarct or hemorrhage but confirmed chronic small vessel disease and an old right-sided infarct. He was bridged to therapeutic anticoagulation with heparin while warfarin dosing was corrected and clarified. His symptoms improved, gait stabilized, and INR reached 2.8 by discharge. New medications for constipation were added, and he was discharged home with updated warfarin instructions, follow-up in the anticoagulation clinic, and continued management of his multiple chronic conditions.
